investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-26T00:27–00:28Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". Because all three sibling checks share the identical error message and all failed within the same ~35-second window, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to individual check logic or eval runner code. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the gateway never responded successfully.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run. All three checks hit the same endpoint and received the same 502 within 35 seconds, which is the strongest indicator of a shared infrastructure failure.

Secondary — Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api and the ELB, causing the connection attempt to fail fast (~11 seconds) rather than waiting for the full outageLatencyMs window.
Tertiary — The ELB target group had zero healthy instances (e.g., swarm worker pods crashed or were being redeployed), causing the load balancer itself to return 502 to the production-api.

Lower probability — A misconfigured or rotated endpoint URL in the production-api's swarm gateway configuration, pointing to a stale or decommissioned ELB. This would produce the same 502 pattern but would be persistent rather than transient.

investigations.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-26T00:27–00:28Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". Because all three sibling checks share the identical error message and all failed within the same ~35-second window, the failure is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to individual check logic or eval runner code. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical 502 message, latencyMs=11096, endedAt=2026-08-26T00:28:18.206Z.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the gateway never responded successfully.
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run. All three checks hit the same endpoint and received the same 502 within 35 seconds, which is the strongest indicator of a shared infrastructure failure.

Secondary — Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api and the ELB, causing the connection attempt to fail fast (~11 seconds) rather than waiting for the full outageLatencyMs window.
Tertiary — The ELB target group had zero healthy instances (e.g., swarm worker pods crashed or were being redeployed), causing the load balancer itself to return 502 to the production-api.

Lower probability — A misconfigured or rotated endpoint URL in the production-api's swarm gateway configuration, pointing to a stale or decommissioned ELB. This would produce the same 502 pattern but would be persistent rather than transient.
